question: PG reconnect under discard-on-cancel: cost of discarding a cancelled PostgreSQL connection and replacing it (TLS off/on, SCRAM), p50/p99 and sustainable cancel+replace rate per core incl. server-side backend fork cost, vs state-tracked reuse
flips_if: >20 ms p50 or <200 cancels/s → state-tracked reuse

hardware.laptop: Intel Core i9-14900HX, P-cores 8 (client) / 10 (server), kernel 6.17, powersave; heavily loaded (loadavg 20-25); postgres:17 = 17.11 Debian/OpenSSL 3.5.7
hardware.kamrui: Intel N95 (4 E-cores), LAN box as weak-VPS stand-in (NOT a VPS), cores 2 (client) / 3 (server); first suite idle (loadavg 0.44), later runs contended by other agents' jobs; postgres:17-alpine = 17.11

measured.conditions: tokio-postgres 0.7.18 (PR #1374 not applied), rustls 0.23.45 aws-lc-rs TLS1.3 P-256 (PG17 offers only prime256v1), SCRAM-SHA-256 4096 iters; loopback, host network; cancelled op = pg_sleep(0.05) in a txn dropped at 2 ms; split = PG on its own core, shared = PG on the client core (1-vCPU box); rate = 16 closed-loop workers x 8 s
measured.client_side_only_discard_ceiling_per_cor: laptop SCRAM/TLS ~530-560/s; N95 SCRAM/TLS ~135-180/s (<200 even with PG on another host)
measured.reuse_correctness: CancelRequest-based reuse: race probe on N95 (24,997 cycles) 21 resets hit by a stray cancel (detected, fell back to discard) and 3 stray cancels landed on the NEXT request after the sentinel passed (SQLSTATE 57014); laptop 0/42,392; N95 suites 1 reset hit/16,843. reuse-wait (no CancelRequest): 0 errors / 13,586 cycles.

decision_effect: ARCHITECTURE §3.7 / INV-NOMUT-C NC3: replace unconditional discard-on-cancel with state-tracked reuse. Proposed NC3 text: "NC3 a resource in D(r) left mid-protocol is quarantined (never handed to another request) and either recovered or discarded. Recovery = drain every outstanding reply to ReadyForQuery WITHOUT a CancelRequest (the in-flight statement is bounded by statement_timeout = op budget ms), ROLLBACK if the server-reported txn status is not I, DISCARD ALL, and invalidate driver-side statement/type caches (session generation bump), all within T_recover = op budget; checkin iff ReadyForQuery ∧ server-reported txn status I ∧ no outstanding replies ∧ all server objects closed. Any error, timeout, COPY in progress, LISTEN or unknown protocol state ⇒ discard; discard sends a CancelRequest (or relies on client_connection_check_interval) so the orphan backend stops. A CancelRequest is never sent on a connection that will be checked back in. Quarantine time and discards are charged to the cancelling principal (NC4)." Also: oracles/cancel-sweep NC3 check stays (checkin predicate unchanged), and gets a new mutation: reuse after CancelRequest ⇒ stray-cancel on the next request must go red; reverse-trigger text in §3.7 becomes 'Reverse to unconditional discard if recovery leaks session state in the cancel sweep or the q3-008 race probe shows next-request hits for reuse-wait'.
rung: measurement grade B (laptop + LAN box standing in for a VPS; both contended at times)
reproduce: on kamrui (copy suite.sh extra.sh race.sh pg.sh certs/ target/release/q3008): ./suite.sh raw/kamrui-N95.jsonl postgres:17-alpine 2 3 1000 8; ./extra.sh raw/kamrui-extra.jsonl postgres:17-alpine 2 3 1000 8; ./race.sh raw/kamrui-race.jsonl postgres:17-alpine 2 3 5000
limits: No real 1-vCPU VPS (a shared vCPU with steal is likely worse than a dedicated N95 core). Laptop heavily loaded (±30% between repeats); later kamrui runs contended by other agents' jobs. PG17 only (no PG18 ssl_groups / X25519MLKEM768, which would add handshake CPU and strengthen the flip). ECDSA cert (RSA dearer). No PgBouncer. Synthetic workload (pg_sleep in a txn). reuse-wait latency = remaining statement time, so it trades CPU for pool occupancy. The stray-cancel mechanism was observed but not root-caused in PG source. tokio-postgres PR #1374 was not applied (DISCARD ALL covers its leak window in the reuse path).
